findings.summary: reply_to on a terminal latest run is ignored and the text starts a new run, per the ADR 0023 §4 table; needs an owner ruling before 4d.4 exposes the route.

The kernel never builds the request digest; 4d.4 must build it in one tested function over conversation_id, text, reply_to and host_context, with a test that one key posted to two conversations is CONFLICT.
post_message does not bound start text; CreateRun does at the route; 4d.4 needs a 422 test for empty and over-4000 bodies.
The /inputs guard test claims a before-and-after replay but checks only after; no HTTP test of the non-requester refusal.
The moved replay check is equivalent but not verbatim (enum is-comparison, early return).
admit_run_in_conversation shares structure with admit_run and repeats the key-reused literal.
admit_run_in_conversation is public and has no owner check; a caller that skipped the flow could link a run into another owner's conversation.
The latest-run choice lives in private _latest; 4d.3 must reuse it exactly.
Contract digest stale after the plan line edit; refresh-task before close.
